status_vocabulary.implemented: Modelled in sim_core: the code stores or computes it and enforces its rules.
status_vocabulary.referenced: The code uses its id but does not model it: no table, no attributes, no rules of its own.
status_vocabulary.planned: Named as a future layer of the game; no code and no fields yet.

sources: 1. Code in sim_core/include and sim_core/src, and the tests in tests/
2. docs/audit/character-core-018724d.md (audit of 018724d); findings fixed in 5847252 are recorded as resolved
meta.id_policy: Every element has a stable dotted id in lowercase snake_case. Once published, ids are never renamed or reused.
meta.scope: Describes the character core as it stands. The rest of the game is named under entities as planned layers and left empty.
meta.notation: Formulas are plain text over element ids or short names. clamp(x, lo, hi) bounds x; round() is std::round (half away from zero). Integer division truncates.

conventions.description: Time is counted in whole weeks since world start; dates before world start are negative. A date has no calendar beyond that.
Length of a year in weeks, the mean Gregorian year. A calendar constant, not a gameplay coefficient.
Durations between dates are signed week counts (positive when the second date is later); years are weeks / WEEKS_PER_YEAR as a double.
conventions.formula: weeks_between(from, to) = to.weeks - from.weeks; weeks_to_years(w) = w / WEEKS_PER_YEAR
conventions.clamps: none; weeks_between asserts in debug that the difference fits int32

conventions.description: Traits, reputation, stances and modifier effects are whole numbers from -100 to +100, stored as the value itself. Fractions never reach them silently: callers round explicitly.
details: set_ clamps any integer argument to -100..+100 with mixed-sign-safe comparisons, so no width or signedness overflows.
add_ clamps the delta to -200..+200 first, then clamps the sum to -100..+100.
Inputs must be StrictIntegral (type.strict_integral): a float, bool or character argument matches no function and does not compile.
-128 is never stored.

conventions.description: Health, stress and capacity are fractional from 0 to 100, kept to the hundredth. They are the only scales with a float interface.
details: set rounds value * 100 to the nearest integer with std::round (half away from zero) after clamping to 0..10000.
Infinities saturate at 0 or 100. NaN leaves the field unchanged (asserted in debug).

add rounds the delta to whole hundredths first (clamped to -10000..+10000), then adds in a wide integer and saturates: the same delta always adds the same steps, and add(d) then add(-d) restores the value unless saturation intervened.
A delta below 0.005 in magnitude rounds away by design.
Getters return raw / 100 as float.

conventions.description: Long-term personal opinions are whole numbers from -200 to +200 so that a strong personal history can outweigh a saturated community stance. 0 means no entry.
details: A single delta is clamped to -400..+400 (LONG_DELTA_MAX) on entry, so one call can cross the whole range.
The stored result is clamped to -200..+200; a result of 0 removes the entry.

conventions.description: A modifier's effect is a whole number from -100 to +100, fixed when the modifier is added; 0 is allowed.
Computed opinions are doubles on the -100..+100 scale. Their terms are not clamped individually; only the totals are. Rounding to whole numbers is the caller's choice.
An involvement share is a fraction weight / total, not a scale; the bipolar and condition rules do not apply to it.
Every id is an opaque unsigned handle of its own type; 0 is the invalid id. Ids of different types never convert into each other or into integers implicitly.
details: CharacterId, NameId, CommunityId and TopicId are u32; SkillId and ModifierId are u16.
valid() is value != 0.

conventions.description: Character ids start at 1, increase by one per created character and are never reused, even after a character is forgotten.
details: create returns the invalid id once 2^31 - 1 ids have been used.
A forgotten id behaves like one never created: exists() is false, queries are empty, edits return NotFound.

conventions.description: A TargetId names a community or a topic as the target of a stance, long opinion, modifier or sacred entry.
conventions.quantization: 2 high bits kind, 30 low bits index
conventions.range: index 1..2^30-1 and a known kind (enforced by TargetId::from and from_raw)
details: Valid iff index != 0; the default TargetId is invalid.
Built only by TargetId::from, which rejects an invalid id and an index >= 2^30 (INDEX_LIMIT).
TargetId::from_raw decodes a stored raw value, rejecting index 0 and unknown kinds.
Ordering is by raw value: grouped by kind, then by index.

conventions.description: Every edit checks its inputs in a fixed order and reports the first failure. A failed edit changes nothing.
order: Invalid: id 0, a == b, unknown enum value, wrong relation kind, invalid TargetId or ModifierId 0
NotFound: a character id never created or forgotten
Invalid: a dead participant where the edit does not allow one (needs a lookup, so it follows NotFound)
Duplicate / Conflict / NotFound against existing state
Full: a storage bound or limit is reached
exceptions: op.kill: a dead id is NotFound, not Invalid; death < birth is Invalid after NotFound.
Long-opinion edits report a LongOpinionOutcome instead of an EditResult.

conventions.description: Edits check everything first, then reserve room in every container they will grow, then write. An allocation failure (std::bad_alloc) is thrown before any write and leaves the world unchanged.
A full list returns Full and is never emptied to make room. Only the long-term opinion lists have gameplay limits with eviction (rule.long.eviction).
conventions.source: CLAUDE.md#Design rules established so far / Per-character lists

conventions.description: Anything read from the registry by reference (pointers, references, spans) is valid only until the next registry mutation: create, kill, maintain, any relation edit or personal opinion edit. Spans into a Character's lists are valid only until the next mutation of that Character. Vectors returned by queries are independent copies.

Opinion math uses only + - * / and comparisons on doubles, never exp, log or pow, so the same world yields bit-identical opinions on every platform under the project's flags (-ffp-contract=off, no fast-math). Golden values in the tests pin it.
All randomness is deterministic noise derived from an explicit world seed and ids; there is no global or hidden random state.
Mortality (exp, log, expm1, log1p), condition getters and involvement_share use float or transcendental math and are not guaranteed bit-identical across platforms.
Nothing in personal or weak opinions depends on time: no dates, no decay, no recalculation. Opinions change only when their inputs are edited.

types.description: Handle of a character, living, dead or forgotten.
Handle of a name or nickname. Names themselves are not modelled.
Handle of a community.
Handle of a topic.
Handle of a skill within a skill kind.
Kind of opinion modifier (an insult, a gift, ...).
Community or topic as a target; see conv.ids.target_id.
A point in time; see conv.time.date.
Seed of all noise in a world. Persistent world state: changing it changes every noise value.
The integer types the model accepts wherever it takes whole numbers: any width and signedness, but no floating point, bool or character types.
Gender of a character. Persisted: append-only.
Kind of skill. Persisted: append-only.
Whether a sacred target is revered (Plus) or abhorred (Minus). Persisted: append-only.
Relation between two characters; the value is also its bit in the edge mask, so at most 32 types. Persisted: append-only. Each value is described under relations.
Whether a relation type is set on one edge or on both.

value_notes.OneWay: set on the source edge only
value_notes.Paired: always set on both edges, with the complement on the reverse edge

types.description: Kind of entity a TargetId names. Stored in 2 bits: append-only, at most 4 kinds; value 2 is intended for persons, 3 is free.
Which id space a modifier's target belongs to, so a character and a community with the same number never collide. Persisted: append-only.

value_notes.Target: target is a TargetId (community or topic)

types.description: Kind of noise target, part of the hash input. Frozen: renumbering shifts the noise of the whole world.
Result of every list, relation and stance edit. Every non-Ok result leaves state unchanged.

value_notes.Ok: the edit was applied (or was a no-op where stated)
value_notes.Full: a new entry was needed but a capacity or limit was reached
value_notes.Duplicate: the entry or bit already exists
value_notes.Conflict: an existing entry or bit contradicts the edit
value_notes.NotFound: unknown character, or removal of an absent entry or bit
value_notes.Invalid: invalid id, enum value or kind, or a dead participant where not allowed

types.description: Result of a long-term opinion edit.

value_notes.Updated: an existing entry changed to another nonzero value
value_notes.CreatedWithEviction: a new entry replaced the weakest one; evicted names it
value_notes.Removed: an existing entry reached 0 and was removed
value_notes.Unchanged: nothing written: a delta of 0, or a value already saturated in that direction
value_notes.Dropped: the list is at its limit and the new entry is not stronger than the weakest
value_notes.Invalid: id 0, a == b, an invalid TargetId, or a dead holder

types.description: Initial values of a new character: three condition values and twelve bipolar values. Lists are not part of it and start empty. Defaults are under config.character_init.
details: Condition values saturate at 0..100; NaN leaves the field at its default (asserted in debug).
Bipolar values are type.bipolar_init.

types.description: Initial value of a bipolar field in CharacterInit. Converts from any StrictIntegral and clamps to -100..+100, so designated initializers cannot truncate a float or wrap a wide integer. Not persistent.

The world-wide inputs an operation reads besides the registry: the stance table, the opinion and lifecycle configs and the world seed. Built at the call site and never stored. MortalityConfig is not part of it.
Result of op.kill: the edit result, the fame stored in the dead record and whether the death is legendary; fame and legendary are meaningful only when result is Ok.
Result of a long-opinion edit: the outcome and, for CreatedWithEviction only, the evicted target (typed like the target; invalid otherwise).
The terms of a weak opinion and their clamped total, for tuning and tooltips.
fields: compat (0 for non-person and dead targets)

types.description: A weak opinion plus the personal terms and the clamped total.
fields: short_term (int, sum of effects, 0 without modifiers)

types.description: Kind and complement of a relation type: the single source of both. Empty for values outside the enum.
fields: complement (empty for one-way types; Spouse is its own complement)

types.description: Relations from one character to another, as returned by relations(a): the other character and a bit mask of the roles the other has for a.
fields: mask (u32, bit relation_bit(t) set when other has role t for a; never 0 when stored)

entities.description: A person in the world: identity, condition, personality, skills, memberships, sacred values and personal opinions. Only the living are characters; at death a character becomes a dead_record.

fields.description: Identity of the character, unique for the whole timeline.

fields.range: unenforced (op.create does not validate it; rule.mortality.annual asserts a known value in debug)

fields.description: Date of birth; may be before world start.
Physical health; low health raises mortality.
Accumulated stress; high stress raises mortality.
Emotional stability (Big Five; the opposite of neuroticism).
Openness to experience (Big Five). Makes opinions of communities and topics more varied.
Extraversion (Big Five). Sets how many people a character keeps long-term opinions about.
Body shape relative to the norm.
How the world regards the character. Feeds everyone's weak opinion of them and their fame at death.
How many living characters remember this character. A dead character nobody remembers is forgotten; at death it sets the base of fame.
fields.type: std::uint32_t per id, held by the registry (not in Character)
fields.note: Maintained incrementally by every reference-changing edit; must equal rule.memory.holders. Kept for living and dead ids; reads 0 for forgotten and unknown ids.

lists.description: Names the character is also known by.
lists.ordering: insertion order (remove keeps the order of the rest)

lists.description: Skills the character has. Skills are capabilities: present or absent, without a level. Query: has_skill(kind, skill).
The communities the character belongs to and how strongly. Weights are relative; the share of a community is its weight over the sum.
lists.duplicates: one entry per community: setting again overwrites the weight
lists.eviction: none: Full when a ninth community is added

range.enforced_by: set_involvement clamps to 0..255; 0 (or a negative weight) removes the entry

lists.description: Communities or topics the character holds sacred (Plus) or abhors (Minus). Flipping a sign takes an explicit removal first. Query: sacred_sign(target).
lists.duplicates: same sign: Duplicate; opposite sign: Conflict

lists.description: What the character has come to think of particular people through personal history. Extraverts remember more people; the weakest memories make way for stronger ones. Entries about the dead are kept and keep them remembered.
lists.duplicates: one entry per target: a new delta adds to the existing value
lists.eviction: rule.long.eviction on insert (one per call); rule.long.trim in op.maintain when the list is above person_limit
lists.note: May exceed person_limit after extraversion is lowered, until op.maintain runs.

entry.description: The person; living or dead, never the owner.
The long-term opinion of that person.

lists.description: What the character has come to think of particular communities and topics through personal history.
lists.duplicates: one entry per target: a new delta adds to the existing value
lists.eviction: rule.long.eviction on insert (one per call); never above the limit (asserted)

entry.description: The long-term opinion of that target.

lists.description: Active circumstances shaping the character's short-term opinion of a person, community or topic (an insult, a gift). Each has an effect fixed when it is added; the same circumstance cannot stack on the same target.

entry.description: Whether the target is a person or a community/topic.
entry.range: set by the edit (person or target overload)

entry.description: The target: a CharacterId (domain Person) or a TargetId (domain Target), read back through person() or target_id().
entry.quantization: CharacterId value or TargetId raw, per domain
entry.range: never 0; Person: valid, != owner, existing; Target: valid TargetId

entry.description: The modifier's effect on the opinion.

derived.description: Age in years at a given date; negative before birth.
Probability of dying within one year at a given date.
Sum of the character's involvement weights.
Share of one community in the character's involvement, for display.
The community the character belongs to most; none without involvement. Recorded at death.
derived.range: a CommunityId from the involvement list, or none

derived.description: How many people the character keeps long-term opinions about.

entities.description: What remains of a character after death: identity, dates, fame and the few values others' opinions of the deceased need. Written once at death and never changed; deleted when nobody remembers the character.

fields.description: Identity of the deceased; same id as in life.
The community the character belonged to most at death; invalid if none. Gives the dead a community for others' opinions.
How famous the deceased was at death.

entities.description: A group a character can belong to (a family, a tribe, a faith). Exists only as an id, its place in the hierarchy and its stances; it has no attributes and no lifecycle (it is never created, killed or forgotten).

parts.description: Communities nest: each has at most one parent, and a community inherits its ancestors' stances where it has none of its own.
parts.duplicates: one parent per child: op.set_community_parent replaces it

entry.description: The community being placed under a parent.

entry.range: valid, != child, no cycle, every chain at most MAX_COMMUNITY_DEPTH long (enforced by op.set_community_parent)

parts.description: Explicit attitudes of a community towards another community (including itself, for in-group cohesion) or a topic. An explicit 0 is a real attitude, not an absence.

entry.description: The community or topic the stance is about.

entities.description: A subject characters and communities hold views on. Exists only as an id inside a TargetId; it has no hierarchy (it walks no chain), no attributes and no lifecycle.
A name or nickname. Characters carry NameIds; the names themselves are not modelled.
A skill, identified by its kind and id. There is no skill table; a character either has a skill or not.

A kind of circumstance that shapes short-term opinion (an insult, a gift). Only its id exists; there is no type table, and each use gives its own effect. The active instances are character.list.modifiers.
Permanent base layer: terrain, elevation, drainage basins.
Time-varying layer on top of geography.
Material records that can preserve the memory of dead characters, mostly famous ones.

relations.description: Relations between two characters live on one edge per ordered pair. A bit on the edge a -> b names b's role for a (Child: b is a's child). Every edge, whatever its bits, makes its living source remember its target.
details: Empty edges are removed.
One-way types touch only a -> b; paired types always change both edges, with the complement on b -> a.
Queries (relations, has_relation, parents, children, siblings, shared_parents) work for living and dead ids and may return dead ids; they are empty for forgotten ids.

relations.exclusivity: none: one-way types never conflict, with each other or with paired types
relations.dead_participants: never: a dead participant is Invalid; edges from and to the deceased are cleared at death

relations.exclusivity: none: one-way types never conflict, with each other or with paired types
relations.dead_participants: never: a dead participant is Invalid; edges from and to the deceased are cleared at death

relations.exclusivity: none: one-way types never conflict, with each other or with paired types
relations.dead_participants: never: a dead participant is Invalid; edges from and to the deceased are cleared at death

relations.description: b is a's parent. Query: parents(a), in id order, may include the dead.
relations.exclusivity: only with its complement on the same edge (Conflict); no limit on how many characters hold this relation
relations.dead_participants: allowed: posthumous links, even between two dead
relations.limits: a has at most MAX_PARENTS (config.constant.max_parents) parents, dead ones included: Full

relations.description: b is a's child. Query: children(a), in id order, may include the dead.
relations.exclusivity: only with its complement on the same edge (Conflict); no limit on how many characters hold this relation
relations.dead_participants: allowed: posthumous links, even between two dead
relations.limits: b has at most MAX_PARENTS (config.constant.max_parents) parents, dead ones included: Full

relations.exclusivity: only with its complement on the same edge (Conflict); no limit on how many characters hold this relation
relations.dead_participants: not allowed (Invalid); unlinked on both sides at death

relations.exclusivity: only with its complement on the same edge (Conflict); no limit on how many characters hold this relation
relations.dead_participants: not allowed (Invalid); unlinked on both sides at death

relations.exclusivity: only with its complement on the same edge (Conflict); no limit on how many characters hold this relation
relations.dead_participants: not allowed (Invalid); unlinked on both sides at death

relations.exclusivity: only with its complement on the same edge (Conflict); no limit on how many characters hold this relation
relations.dead_participants: not allowed (Invalid); unlinked on both sides at death

relations.description: a and b are married. Spouse is its own complement.
relations.exclusivity: none: Spouse is its own complement, so it never conflicts; no limit on the number of spouses
relations.dead_participants: allowed: posthumous links, even between two dead

relations.description: Characters sharing at least one parent with a. Never stored; derived from parent links, so siblings through a dead parent keep working while the parent is remembered.
relations.formula: siblings(a) = sorted unique { c : c != a and c is a Child of some p in parents(a) }

relations.description: How many parents two characters share: 2 for full siblings, 1 for half siblings, 0 otherwise (also for a == b or unknown ids).
relations.formula: shared_parents(a, b) = |{ p in parents(a) : p in parents(b) }|

rules.description: Where a community looks for stances: itself first, then its parent, grandparent and so on. A topic has no chain.
rules.formula: chain(c) = [c, parent(c), parent(parent(c)), ...] (at most MAX_COMMUNITY_DEPTH); target_chain(community t) = chain(t) as TargetIds, skipping ancestors with id >= 2^30; target_chain(topic t) = [t]; invalid id -> []
rules.clamps: length at most MAX_COMMUNITY_DEPTH (guaranteed by op.set_community_parent)

rules.description: The stance of a community towards a target is the nearest explicit attitude, looking first through the holder's own ancestry and, for each, through the target's ancestry. The source side wins: a family's own feud overrides its tribe's attitude, and a tribe's stance towards another tribe reaches that tribe's families.
rules.formula: stance(from, to) = for s in chain(from), nearest first: for u in target_chain(to), nearest first: if explicit(s, u) exists return it; else 0
rules.clamps: none needed: stored values are already -100..+100; an invalid id yields 0

rules.description: How well two personalities fit: identical personalities like each other most, opposite extremes least.
rules.formula: compat(A, B) = k_compat * (1 - 2 * D / (200 * W)), D = sum_t w_t * |A.t - B.t|, W = sum_t w_t, t in {stability, openness, extraversion, conscientiousness, agreeableness}
rules.clamps: none; with weights >= 0 the result lies in -k_compat..+k_compat. Weights >= 0 and W > 0 are asserted in debug; in release W <= 0 returns 0

rules.description: Open characters hold more varied views of communities and topics: their noise is scaled up.
rules.formula: openness_factor(A) = openness_factor_min + (openness_factor_max - openness_factor_min) * (A.openness + 100) / 200
rules.clamps: none

rules.description: Individual variation: a fixed, directed pseudo-random value per (world, holder, target), so two characters with the same background still differ, and A's view of B differs from B's view of A.
rules.formula: h = splitmix64(seed); h = splitmix64(h xor source_id); h = splitmix64(h xor ((subject << 32) | target)); noise = (h >> 11) / (2^53 - 1) * 2 - 1
rules.clamps: result in [-1, 1] by construction
rules.frozen: The hash and the NoiseSubject values are frozen: changing either shifts the noise of the whole world; golden values in the tests pin it.

rules.description: What a living character thinks of another living character without personal history: their communities' stances towards each other, the target's reputation, personality fit and individual noise.
rules.formula: community = sum_i sum_j wA_i * wB_j * stance(cA_i -> cB_j) / (totalA * totalB) (0 if either total is 0; a target community id >= 2^30 contributes 0); reputation = k_rep * B.reputation; compat = compat(A, B); noise = k_noise * noise(seed, A.id, Person, B.id); total = clamp(community + reputation + compat + noise, -100, 100)
rules.clamps: only the total, to -100..+100; the community sum is exact integer arithmetic divided once; A == B is asserted in debug and returns all zeros

rules.description: What a living character thinks of a dead one without personal history: stances towards the deceased's main community, frozen reputation and the same noise as in life; personality fit no longer counts.
rules.formula: community = sum_i wA_i * stance(cA_i -> D.main_community) / totalA (0 without a main community or involvement); reputation = k_rep * D.reputation; compat = 0; noise = k_noise * noise(seed, A.id, Person, D.id); total = clamp(sum, -100, 100)
rules.clamps: only the total, to -100..+100; A.id == D.id is asserted in debug and returns all zeros
rules.note: A dead holder cannot be passed: a DeadRecord is not a Character.

rules.description: What a character thinks of a community or topic without personal history: its communities' stances, plus noise scaled by its openness.
rules.formula: community = sum_i wA_i * stance(cA_i -> T) / totalA (0 without involvement); reputation = 0; compat = 0; noise = k_noise * openness_factor(A) * noise(seed, A.id, Community|Topic, T.index); total = clamp(sum, -100, 100)
rules.clamps: only the total, to -100..+100; an invalid target returns all zeros

rules.description: The stored long-term opinion of a target, or 0 without an entry.
rules.formula: long(A, X) = value of A's entry about X in long_opinions_people (persons, living or dead) or long_opinions_targets (communities, topics), else 0
rules.clamps: stored values are -200..+200

rules.description: The combined effect of the character's active modifiers on a target.
rules.formula: short(A, X) = sum of effect over A's modifiers with (domain, target) = X
rules.clamps: none: a raw sum, at most MODIFIER_CAP * 100 in magnitude; only the total opinion is clamped

rules.description: A character's full opinion of a person (living or dead), community or topic: the weak opinion plus personal history. Because the weak total is clamped first, personal history can pull an opinion back from a saturated community stance.
rules.formula: opinion(A, X) = clamp(weak(A -> X).total + long(A, X) + short(A, X), -100, 100), with weak = rule.opinion.weak_person, rule.opinion.weak_dead or rule.opinion.weak_target by target
rules.clamps: weak total clamped to -100..+100, then the sum clamped to -100..+100; A == X or an invalid target returns the (zero) weak breakdown
rules.note: Nothing is stored or cached. Relations do not affect weak or personal opinions.

rules.description: Extraverts keep long-term opinions about more people: 8 at extraversion -100, 24 at 0, 40 at +100.
rules.formula: person_limit(A) = PERSON_LIMIT_MIN + (32 * (A.extraversion + 100) + 100) / 200, with 32 = PERSON_LIMIT_MAX - PERSON_LIMIT_MIN (integer arithmetic, round half up)
rules.clamps: none needed: 8..40 by construction

rules.description: How a long-term opinion changes: deltas add up, saturate at +-200, and an opinion that returns to 0 is forgotten as an entry.
rules.formula: existing entry: next = clamp(value + delta, -200, 200); next == value -> Unchanged; next == 0 -> Removed; else Updated. No entry: delta == 0 -> Unchanged; value = clamp(delta, -200, 200); list below its limit -> Created; else rule.long.eviction
rules.clamps: delta clamped to -400..+400 on entry; value clamped to -200..+200

rules.description: When a character's long-term list is full, a new opinion replaces the weakest one only if it is strictly stronger; otherwise it is dropped.
rules.formula: if size >= limit: w = entry with smallest |value| (ties to the smaller target); if |new| > |w.value|: remove w, insert new -> CreatedWithEviction (evicted = w.target); else Dropped. limit = person_limit (people) or TARGET_LIMIT (targets)
rules.clamps: one eviction per call, even if the list is above its limit
rules.note: Modifiers count towards neither the limits nor an entry's strength.

rules.description: Brings a people list back within its limit after extraversion dropped, forgetting the weakest opinions first.
rules.formula: while size > person_limit(A): remove the entry with smallest |value| (ties to the smaller target); report evicted targets in eviction order
rules.clamps: idempotent; target lists never exceed TARGET_LIMIT (asserted)

rules.description: Total weight of a character's memberships.
rules.formula: involvement_total(A) = sum of weights
rules.clamps: none: 0..8*255 by construction

rules.description: The share of one community in a character's memberships, for display. Weighted sums elsewhere use raw weights and divide once.
rules.formula: share(A, c) = weight(c) / involvement_total(A), computed in double and returned as float; 0 if absent
rules.clamps: never adjusted to force an exact sum, so equal weights give equal shares

rules.description: The community a character belongs to most.
rules.formula: main_community(A) = community with the largest weight, ties to the smaller id; none without involvement
rules.clamps: none

rules.description: A character's age at a date.
rules.formula: age_years(A, now) = weeks_between(A.birth, now) / WEEKS_PER_YEAR
rules.clamps: none; negative before birth

rules.description: The yearly chance of death grows exponentially with age (Gompertz), differs by gender and rises with poor health and high stress. Mortality never kills anyone by itself: the caller rolls and calls op.kill.
rules.formula: if age < 0: 0. hazard = gompertz_a * exp(gompertz_b * age) * gender_multiplier * exp(health_weight * (1 - health / 100)) * exp(stress_weight * stress / 100), summed in log space; p = 1 - exp(-hazard)
rules.clamps: NaN (only from an invalid config) maps to 0; p is capped at 1; gompertz_a >= 0 and multipliers >= 0 are asserted in debug
rules.note: An unknown Gender asserts in debug and uses multiplier 1.0 in release. Plain Gompertz has no infant or child mortality peak.

rules.description: Converts a yearly death probability to a weekly one with the same compounded risk.
rules.formula: weekly(annual) = 1 - (1 - annual)^(1 / WEEKS_PER_YEAR)
rules.clamps: annual <= 0 -> 0; annual >= 1 -> 1; NaN asserted in debug and maps to 0 in release

rules.description: Who remembers a character: the living characters with a long-term opinion of them, a modifier about them, or any relation edge towards them. Several references from one holder count once; the dead remember nobody; opinions of communities and topics are not references to characters.
rules.formula: holders(X) = |{ living H != X : X in H.long_opinions_people or H has a Person modifier on X or edge H -> X exists }|
rules.clamps: none
rules.maintenance: Incremental and flip-driven: an edit consults the other reference kinds only when it creates or removes the first or last reference of its own kind for that pair (an edge created or erased, the first or last person modifier on X, a long entry created, removed or evicted). Changing bits on an existing edge or adding a second modifier costs no lookups.

rules.description: A dead character nobody living remembers is forgotten at once: its record is deleted and its id behaves as if it had never existed. A dead parent is remembered while any of its children lives.
rules.formula: when holders(X) reaches 0 and X is dead: delete X's dead_record, remove X's remaining edges on both sides (only with other dead characters), mark X forgotten
rules.clamps: several forgettings caused by one change happen in id order; forgetting never cascades (no living holder changes) and never allocates
triggers: op.kill (the deceased itself if nobody holds it, and dead characters only the deceased held)
rules.note: Legendary characters are forgotten like everyone else.

rules.description: How famous a character was at death: how many people remembered them, plus how far their reputation was from neutral.
rules.formula: fame = min(holders(X) just before the kill + fame_per_reputation * |X.reputation|, 65535)
rules.clamps: saturates at 65535

rules.description: A death is legendary when fame reaches a threshold. Only reported by op.kill, for a later system to react to; it changes nothing in the core.
rules.formula: legendary = fame >= legendary_fame
rules.clamps: none

rules.description: Opinions do not jump at death: each living character with a long-term opinion of the deceased has it shifted by the change in their weak opinion, so the total stays within half a point unless the long value saturates. Without a long entry the opinion moves to the dead-record base.
rules.formula: for each living holder H with a long entry about X: delta = round(weak_person(H, X alive).total - weak_dead(H, X record).total), clamped to -400..+400; apply rule.long.update (a result of 0 removes the entry; a saturated value is Unchanged)
rules.clamps: delta rounded with std::round and clamped to -400..+400; long value clamped to -200..+200

rules.description: At death family ties stay; service and personal ties end.
rules.formula: survives_death (Parent, Child, Spouse): kept on both sides; other paired types (Liege, Vassal, Employer, Employee): unlinked on both sides; one-way types from and to the deceased: cleared
rules.clamps: none

rules.description: The dead remember nobody: the deceased's own long-term opinions and modifiers are discarded and stop counting towards others' holders. Others' modifiers about the deceased stay.
rules.formula: for each distinct person target Y of X's long entries, person modifiers and edges: holders(Y) -= 1; then X's Character, with its lists, is replaced by its dead_record
rules.clamps: none

extension_points.description: Character and world generation. The core only creates characters from explicit initial values; seeds and configs are always passed in, never drawn from hidden state.
Time advancing and events. Nothing in the core runs on its own: mortality produces probabilities but never kills, and ticks are expected only to add or remove modifiers.

extension_points.description: Saving and loading. Persisted enums are marked append-only and persistent state is kept free of pointers and floating point, but there is no save or load code.
Binding to a game engine. No engine is chosen; the core uses no engine types.
Names. Characters carry NameIds only; there is no name table or pool.
Conversion of short-term modifiers into long-term opinion. Long values change only through add_long_opinion for now.

discrepancies.description: A comment in the Character constructor says the registry is 'a later step'. The registry exists and is the only creator of characters.

bipolar.hpp says every bipolar scale, including 'later opinions', is a whole number in -100..+100 stored directly. In the code, computed opinions are doubles that are never stored, and long-term values are whole numbers in -200..+200.
The EditResult comment gives the check order as Invalid, NotFound, Duplicate/Conflict/NotFound, Full. The registry also returns Invalid for a dead participant between NotFound and the state checks.
The LongOpinionOutcome::Invalid comment lists 'id 0, a == b, or an invalid TargetId'. The registry also returns Invalid for a dead holder.
The registry's personal-opinion comment gives NotFound as 'an id never created'. The code also returns NotFound for forgotten ids, as CLAUDE.md states.

Two CLAUDE.md paragraphs are corrupted by markdown: the dead-record base formula renders as 'sum*c share_A(c) ... main*community(D) ... k_noise \* noise' and the byte-determinism paragraph has a misplaced backtick. The intended text matches the code.
discrepancies.source: CLAUDE.md#Design rules established so far / Death ; CLAUDE.md#Design rules established so far / Byte determinism

open_questions.description: MortalityConfig is passed to annual_mortality on its own and is not part of WorldContext, unlike the opinion and lifecycle configs. Is this intended?

Paired types conflict only with their own complement on the same edge. A character can have any number of spouses, lieges or employers, a pair can be spouses and liege/vassal at once, and one-way Friend and Rival can sit on the same edge. Is that intended?
create accepts NameId 0 and any Gender value without a check, while nickname edits reject NameId 0 and annual_mortality asserts a known Gender. Is that intended?

weekly_mortality converts an annual probability, but the code never connects it to annual_mortality: the caller does. character.derived.annual_mortality therefore lists no user, and rule.mortality.weekly does not list it as an input.
Modifiers do not expire, and others' modifiers about the deceased stay at death, so a single modifier keeps a dead character remembered for as long as its holder lives. Is that intended?
